standard_prerequisites.name: The same-chapter equivalence between quasi-coherent modules on a closed subscheme and quasi-coherent modules on the ambient scheme annihilated by the ideal sheaf, which gives the uniqueness in the form used here
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited at proof lines 964-967 and again at 969-970
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the condition that the module is pushed forward from a closed subscheme into a statement about the annihilator, and gives uniqueness of the pushed forward module.

standard_prerequisites.name: The same-chapter bijection between closed subschemes of an affine scheme and ideals of the coordinate ring, used to see that the annihilator rule defines a closed subscheme
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the existence of the smallest closed subscheme to showing that the annihilator rule gives a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals.

standard_prerequisites.name: Over an affine scheme a finite type quasi-coherent module is the tilde of a finite module, and the image of the support of the module is the closed subset defined by the annihilator
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the finiteness of the pushed forward module and the identification of supports.

core_obligations: Uniqueness and minimality: if a closed subscheme satisfies the affine annihilator description then the module is the pushforward of a unique quasi-coherent module on it, and the same equivalence shows that a closed subscheme with this property is the smallest one possible (proof lines 964-970).
Finiteness and support: the pushed forward module is of finite type and its support agrees with the support of the original module (proof lines 971-978).

Existence: it remains to show that the affine annihilator rule defines a closed subscheme, for which it suffices to see that the rule produces a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals; this reduces to the algebra statement that the annihilator of a finite module commutes with localization at an element (proof lines 979-986).
proof_roadmap: Use the closed subscheme/quasi-coherent-module equivalence to get uniqueness, minimality, finiteness and the support statement (proof lines 964-978).
Reduce existence to the quasi-coherence of the annihilator ideal, which is the localization compatibility of annihilators of finite modules (proof lines 979-986).
difficulty_reason: The lemma constructs the scheme theoretic support of a finite type quasi-coherent module as the smallest closed subscheme from which the module can be pushed forward, and states its affine description by annihilators together with uniqueness, finiteness and the identification of supports (statement lines 945-961). The counted proof uses the closed subscheme/module equivalence to obtain uniqueness and minimality, the affine dictionary to get finiteness and supports, and then reduces the existence of the closed subscheme to the quasi-coherence of the annihilator ideal, which is the compatibility of annihilators of finite modules with localization (proof lines 963-986). It is H2: the organisation of the argument is carried out in the counted span; the only thing the author leaves to the reader is the elementary localization statement, which is named explicitly in the span.
